method.label: Count exponent choices and subtract overlap

annotationRationale: Prime exponents characterize square and cube divisors. Independent exponent choices give the counts, and two-set inclusion-exclusion removes the duplicated sixth powers.
sourceMethod: Follows the official prime-exponent enumeration of squares, cubes, and sixth powers, followed by subtraction of the overlap.

review.mathCheck: Since 201^9=3^9·67^9, square divisors have 5 choices per exponent and cube divisors have 4. Their intersection has exponents in {0,6}, giving 25+16−4=37, choice C. Zero exponents correctly include 1.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 11 on page 5, using prime-exponent choices and subtracting the sixth-power overlap.
review.annotationCheck: Assessed divisor counting, exponent structure, and union counting are appropriate; multiplication is valid supporting knowledge. Divisor sums are not assessed.
